rules.rule_name: Program Execution Start Announcement
rules.rule_description: The program announces the beginning of its execution by displaying a start message before any customer data processing begins.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1: Display Start Message
CBCUS01C Execution Begins

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer File Display Program CBCUS01C is invoked
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins execution
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBCUS01C' is displayed to the output before any file operations or customer record processing takes place

rules.rule_name: Customer File Open for Sequential Reading
rules.rule_description: The Customer File (CUSTFILE) must be opened for sequential input reading as the first file operation before any customer records can be accessed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2: Open Customer File
Open CUSTFILE for Sequential Reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has displayed its start message and is ready to begin customer record processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE) for sequential input reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer File is opened in INPUT mode to allow sequential reading of all customer records, and the file open status is evaluated to determine if the operation was successful

rules.rule_name: Customer File Open Success Validation
rules.rule_description: After attempting to open the Customer File, the program validates whether the file was opened successfully before proceeding to read customer records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
File Opened
Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE) for input reading
acceptance_criteria.When: The file open operation completes and the file status is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file status indicates success (status code '00'), the application result is set to zero (AOK) and the program proceeds to the sequential record processing loop; otherwise, the application result is set to 12 (error) and the file open error reporting process is triggered

rules.rule_name: Customer File Open Error Reporting and Program Termination
rules.rule_description: When the Customer File cannot be opened successfully, the program reports the error with the file status details and terminates abnormally, preventing any customer record processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9: File Open Error Reporting
Display Error Message with File Status
Terminate Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program attempted to open the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE) and the file open operation did not return a successful status
acceptance_criteria.When: The file open failure is detected (application result is not AOK)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE' is displayed, the file status is captured and displayed in a formatted status message prefixed with 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN', and the program is terminated abnormally by calling the system abend routine CEE3ABD with abend code 999

rules.rule_name: Sequential Customer Record Processing Loop
rules.rule_description: The program processes all customer records sequentially in a continuous loop, reading and displaying each record until the end of the Customer File is reached.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3: Sequential Customer Record
Processing Loop
Process All Records Until End-of-File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer File has been successfully opened for sequential reading and the End-of-File indicator is set to 'N'
acceptance_criteria.When: The sequential processing loop is active
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program continuously reads and processes customer records one at a time, repeating the read-and-display cycle until the End-of-File indicator is set to 'Y', at which point the loop terminates and the program proceeds to close the Customer File

rules.rule_name: End-of-File Condition Check Before Reading
rules.rule_description: At each iteration of the processing loop, the program checks whether the end of the Customer File has been reached before attempting to read the next record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
End of File
Reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The sequential customer record processing loop is active
acceptance_criteria.When: Each iteration of the loop begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the End-of-File indicator is 'N' (end of file not yet reached), the program proceeds to read the next customer record; if the End-of-File indicator is 'Y' (end of file reached), the loop exits and the program proceeds to close the Customer File

rules.rule_name: Read Next Sequential Customer Record
rules.rule_description: The program reads the next sequential customer record from the Customer File into the Customer Record data area for processing and display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4: Read Next Customer Record
Read Next Sequential Record from File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The End-of-File indicator is 'N' and the program is within the sequential processing loop
acceptance_criteria.When: The program executes a sequential read operation on the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next customer record is read from the Customer File into the CUSTOMER-RECORD data area, and the resulting file status is evaluated to determine whether the read was successful, end-of-file was reached, or an unexpected error occurred

rules.rule_name: Customer Record Read Status Evaluation
rules.rule_description: After each read operation, the program evaluates the file status to determine whether a customer record was successfully retrieved, the end of file was reached, or an unexpected error occurred.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Read
Successful?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Customer File
acceptance_criteria.When: The file status returned from the read operation is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file status is '00' (successful read), the application result is set to zero (AOK) and the customer record is displayed; if the file status is '10' (end of file), the application result is set to 16 (EOF) and the End-of-File indicator is set to 'Y' to stop the loop; if the file status is any other value (unexpected error), the application result is set to 12 (error) and the read error reporting process is triggered

rules.rule_name: Display Successfully Retrieved Customer Record
rules.rule_description: When a customer record is successfully read from the Customer File, the complete customer record details are displayed to the output.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5: Display Customer Record
Print Customer Record Details to Output

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential read operation on the Customer File has returned a successful status (file status '00') and the CUSTOMER-RECORD data area has been populated with the retrieved record
acceptance_criteria.When: The successful read is confirmed (application result is AOK)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete contents of the CUSTOMER-RECORD are displayed to the output, and the processing loop continues to check for the next record

rules.rule_name: End-of-File Indicator Setting to Stop Processing Loop
rules.rule_description: When the read operation detects that there are no more customer records in the file, the End-of-File indicator is set to stop the processing loop gracefully.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6: End of File Detection
Set End-of-File Indicator = Y
Stop Processing Loop

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential read operation on the Customer File has returned an end-of-file status (file status '10'), setting the application result to 16 (EOF)
acceptance_criteria.When: The application result is evaluated and identified as EOF (application result equals 16)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End-of-File indicator (END-OF-FILE) is set to 'Y', which causes the sequential processing loop to exit on its next iteration check, and the program proceeds to close the Customer File — no error is raised as end-of-file is the expected normal conclusion of processing

rules.rule_name: Unexpected Customer Record Read Error Detection
rules.rule_description: When a read operation on the Customer File returns an unexpected error status (neither successful nor end-of-file), the error condition is detected and escalated for reporting and program termination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7: Read Error Detection
Unexpected Error Encountered

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential read operation on the Customer File has returned a file status that is neither '00' (success) nor '10' (end of file), resulting in an application result of 12 (error)
acceptance_criteria.When: The application result is evaluated and identified as neither AOK nor EOF
acceptance_criteria.Then: The unexpected read error condition is confirmed and the read error reporting and program termination process is immediately triggered

rules.rule_name: Customer File Read Error Reporting and Program Termination
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading a customer record, the program reports the error with file status details and terminates abnormally to prevent processing of potentially corrupt or incomplete data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: File Read Error Reporting
Display Error Message with File Status
Terminate Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unexpected error has been detected during a sequential read operation on the Customer File (application result is 12, indicating neither a successful read nor end-of-file)
acceptance_criteria.When: The read error condition is confirmed and error reporting is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE' is displayed, the file status is captured and displayed in a formatted status message prefixed with 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN', and the program is terminated abnormally by calling the system abend routine CEE3ABD with abend code 999

rules.rule_name: Customer File Close After All Records Processed
rules.rule_description: After all customer records have been read and displayed (end of file reached), the Customer File must be properly closed to complete the processing cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8: Close Customer File
Close CUSTFILE After All Records Processed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The sequential processing loop has exited because the End-of-File indicator was set to 'Y', indicating all customer records have been processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program executes the close operation on the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer File is closed and the resulting file status is evaluated to determine whether the close operation was successful or failed

rules.rule_name: Customer File Close Success Validation
rules.rule_description: After attempting to close the Customer File, the program validates whether the file was closed successfully before announcing program completion.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
File Closed
Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE) after all records have been processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The file close operation completes and the file status is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file status indicates success (status code '00'), the application result is set to zero (AOK) and the program proceeds to display the completion message and exit normally; otherwise, the application result is set to 12 (error) and the file close error reporting process is triggered

rules.rule_name: Customer File Close Error Reporting and Program Termination
rules.rule_description: When the Customer File cannot be closed successfully after all records have been processed, the program reports the error with file status details and terminates abnormally.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: File Close Error Reporting
Display Error Message with File Status
Terminate Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program attempted to close the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE) after completing all record processing and the file close operation did not return a successful status (application result is 12)
acceptance_criteria.When: The file close failure is detected (application result is not AOK)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE' is displayed, the file status is captured and displayed in a formatted status message prefixed with 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN', and the program is terminated abnormally by calling the system abend routine CEE3ABD with abend code 999

rules.rule_name: Program Completion Announcement and Normal Exit
rules.rule_description: Upon successful completion of all customer record processing and successful closure of the Customer File, the program announces its completion and returns control to the calling environment.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12: Program Completion
Display End Message
Return Control to Calling Environment

acceptance_criteria.Given: All customer records have been read and displayed, and the Customer File has been successfully closed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reaches its normal completion point
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBCUS01C' is displayed to the output, and control is returned to the calling environment via GOBACK, signaling successful completion of the customer file display process

rules.rule_name: Customer File Sequential Access Initiation
rules.rule_description: Before any customer records can be retrieved and processed, the Customer File must be opened to enable sequential reading from the beginning of the file through to the last record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Open Customer File for Sequential Reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer File processing is about to begin and no customer records have yet been read
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initiates the Customer File opening sequence to prepare for sequential record retrieval
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer File is opened in read-only sequential access mode, making all customer records available for processing from the first record to the last

rules.rule_name: Customer File Availability Verification
rules.rule_description: After attempting to open the Customer File, the program must verify whether the file is available and accessible. A successful open confirms the file is ready; any other outcome indicates the file is unavailable for processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Customer File Opened Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: An attempt has been made to open the Customer File for sequential reading
acceptance_criteria.When: The result of the file open operation is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Customer File opened successfully, it is marked as ready for sequential record processing; if the Customer File could not be opened for any reason, it is flagged as unavailable and error handling is triggered

rules.rule_name: Customer File Ready for Record Processing
rules.rule_description: When the Customer File has been confirmed as successfully opened, it is designated as ready, allowing the main processing loop to begin retrieving customer records sequentially.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Customer File Ready for Sequential Record Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer File open operation has been evaluated
acceptance_criteria.When: The Customer File has been confirmed as successfully opened with no errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer File is marked as available and ready, and control is returned to the main process to begin sequential customer record retrieval

rules.rule_name: Customer File Open Failure Notification
rules.rule_description: When the Customer File cannot be opened, a descriptive error message must be displayed along with the specific file status details to identify the nature of the failure, enabling diagnosis of why the customer data is inaccessible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display File Open Error Message with File Status Details

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer File open operation has been evaluated and the file could not be opened successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The file open failure condition is confirmed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE' is displayed, followed by the detailed file status information formatted as a 4-character status code prefixed with 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN', so that the reason for the Customer File being unavailable is clearly communicated

rules.rule_name: Program Termination on Customer File Open Failure
rules.rule_description: If the Customer File cannot be opened, the program cannot proceed with any customer record processing. The program must be immediately and abnormally terminated to prevent any further processing without valid customer data access.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Terminate Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer File could not be opened and the file open error message with status details has been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program determines it cannot continue without access to the Customer File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program is immediately terminated abnormally with abend code 999, halting all further customer record processing

rules.rule_name: Loop Entry Control - Check If All Customer Records Have Been Processed
rules.rule_description: Before each iteration of the customer record processing loop, the system checks whether the end-of-file indicator has been set, to determine if all customer records have already been read and no further processing is needed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End of File Indicator = Y?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer record processing loop is active and the system is about to begin or continue an iteration
acceptance_criteria.When: The End-of-File Indicator is evaluated at the start of each loop iteration
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the End-of-File Indicator equals 'Y', the loop exits immediately and processing proceeds to close the Customer File; if the End-of-File Indicator does not equal 'Y', the loop continues to the next check

rules.rule_name: Loop Safety Guard - Confirm File Still Has Unread Records Before Reading
rules.rule_description: As a secondary safety check within the loop, the system confirms the End-of-File Indicator is explicitly set to 'N' before attempting to read the next customer record, preventing any unintended read attempts.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End of File Indicator = N?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The End-of-File Indicator has been confirmed as not equal to 'Y' and the loop is continuing
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the End-of-File Indicator is explicitly equal to 'N'
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the End-of-File Indicator equals 'N', the system proceeds to read the next customer record; if the End-of-File Indicator is not 'N', the system loops back to the primary end-of-file check without reading any record

rules.rule_name: Sequential Customer Record Retrieval
rules.rule_description: The system retrieves the next available customer record sequentially from the Customer File, loading the full customer record details into the active customer record area for processing and display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Next Customer Record from File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer File is open, the End-of-File Indicator is 'N', and there are potentially more customer records to be read
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads the next sequential record from the Customer File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The customer record details are loaded into the Customer Record area and the outcome of the read operation (success, end of file, or error) is captured for subsequent decision-making

rules.rule_name: Successful Customer Record Read - Display Record
rules.rule_description: When a customer record is successfully retrieved from the Customer File, the system displays the full customer record details. Due to the program structure, each successfully read customer record is displayed twice — once immediately upon successful retrieval and once again in the main processing loop after the read operation returns.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Customer Record Details

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Customer File
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation completes successfully, confirming a valid customer record has been retrieved
acceptance_criteria.Then: The full Customer Record details are displayed immediately upon successful retrieval; additionally, since the End-of-File Indicator remains 'N' after a successful read, the Customer Record details are displayed a second time in the main processing loop, resulting in each customer record being displayed twice per successful read

rules.rule_name: End of Customer File Detection - Stop Reading Loop
rules.rule_description: When the system determines that there are no more customer records available in the Customer File, it marks the End-of-File Indicator to signal that all records have been processed and the reading loop should terminate.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark End of File Indicator = Y

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Customer File
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation returns an end-of-file condition, indicating no further customer records exist in the file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End-of-File Indicator is set to 'Y', which causes the processing loop to exit on its next iteration check, and no customer record is displayed for this condition

rules.rule_name: Unexpected Customer File Read Failure - Report Error and Terminate
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading a customer record — any condition other than a successful read or a normal end-of-file — the system reports the error and terminates the program abnormally to prevent processing of incomplete or corrupt customer data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Report Read Error and Terminate Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Customer File
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation returns any outcome other than success or end-of-file, indicating an unexpected failure condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE', displays the file status details, and terminates the program abnormally — no further customer records are read or displayed

rules.rule_name: Loop Exit and Transition to File Closure
rules.rule_description: Once the End-of-File Indicator is confirmed as 'Y', the customer record processing loop exits and control is passed to the file closure process, ensuring the Customer File is properly closed after all records have been processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Exit Loop Proceed to Close File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer record processing loop is evaluating the End-of-File Indicator
acceptance_criteria.When: The End-of-File Indicator equals 'Y', confirming all customer records have been read
acceptance_criteria.Then: The processing loop terminates and the system proceeds to close the Customer File, with no further customer records being read or displayed

rules.rule_description: The system retrieves the next available customer record sequentially from the Customer File and loads it into the customer record structure for downstream processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Next Sequential Record from Customer File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer File has been successfully opened and is ready for sequential reading, and the end-of-file indicator is set to 'N' (more records may exist)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system requests the next sequential customer record from the Customer File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next customer record is read from the Customer File and its data is loaded into the customer record structure, making all customer fields available for processing and display

rules.rule_name: Successful Customer Record Retrieved

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Successfully Retrieved into Customer Record Structure

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed against the Customer File
acceptance_criteria.When: The Customer File returns a successful read result indicating the record was found and retrieved without any issues
acceptance_criteria.Then: The customer record is confirmed as successfully retrieved into the customer record structure, the processing result is marked as successful (no error), and the full customer record details are displayed to the output

rules.rule_name: End-of-File Detection — No More Customer Records
rules.rule_description: When the Customer File signals that there are no more records to read, the system marks the end-of-file indicator to stop further reading and gracefully conclude the processing loop.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark End-of-File Indicator — No More Records to Process

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed against the Customer File and the read was not successful
acceptance_criteria.When: The Customer File signals that the end of the file has been reached and there are no more customer records available to read
acceptance_criteria.Then: The processing result is marked as end-of-file, and the end-of-file indicator is set to 'Y', signalling the processing loop to stop reading and proceed to file closure — no error is raised as this is the expected normal conclusion of processing

rules.rule_name: Unexpected Customer Record Read Failure
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading a customer record — one that is neither a successful read nor a normal end-of-file — the system treats it as a critical failure, displays a diagnostic error message, and terminates the program abnormally.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Read Error — Unexpected Failure Occurred

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed against the Customer File and the read was not successful
acceptance_criteria.When: The Customer File returns an unexpected error result that is neither a successful record retrieval nor a normal end-of-file condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: The processing result is marked as an error, the message 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE' is displayed, the file status details are displayed for diagnostic purposes, and the program is terminated abnormally — no further customer records are processed

rules.rule_name: Validate Successful Customer Record Read Before Display
rules.rule_description: After attempting to read a customer record, the system must verify that the read operation completed successfully before proceeding to display the record. Only a fully successful retrieval qualifies the record for output.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Status Successful?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been attempted on the Customer File to retrieve the next customer record
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation completes and the file status is evaluated — status '00' indicates a successful record retrieval, status '10' indicates end of file has been reached, and any other status indicates a read failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: Only if the read status is '00' (successful record retrieved) is the record considered valid and eligible for display; if the status is '10' (end of file) or any other value (read failure), the record is not eligible for display and processing continues to the next step without displaying any record

rules.rule_name: Verify End-of-File Indicator Before Displaying Customer Record
rules.rule_description: Before displaying a customer record in the main processing loop, the system must confirm that the end-of-file condition has not been reached. This prevents displaying stale or invalid data after the last record has been processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End of File Indicator = N?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record read attempt has been performed and the read paragraph has completed execution
acceptance_criteria.When: The main processing loop evaluates the End-of-File indicator after returning from the read operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the End-of-File indicator is 'N' (more records are available and the last read was successful), the customer record is eligible for display; if the End-of-File indicator is 'Y' (end of file has been reached during the read), the customer record is not displayed and the loop proceeds toward termination

rules.rule_name: Display Full Customer Record Details After Successful Read
rules.rule_description: When a customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer File and the end-of-file condition has not been triggered, the complete customer record details must be printed to the output. This is the core output action of the customer file display process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

Print Full Customer Record to Output

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully read from the Customer File (read status is '00') and the End-of-File indicator remains 'N' after the read operation completes
acceptance_criteria.When: Both the successful read condition and the active (non-end-of-file) processing condition are confirmed true in the main processing loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete customer record details are displayed to the output in full; after display, processing continues to attempt reading the next customer record in the sequence

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must recognise and record an end-of-file condition internally, distinguishing it from a successful record retrieval and from any unexpected read error

rules.rule_name: Set End-of-File Indicator to Stop Processing Loop

acceptance_criteria.Then: The end-of-file indicator must be set to YES, signalling that no further customer records should be requested

rules.rule_name: Exit Customer Record Processing Loop When End-of-File Indicator Is Set
rules.rule_description: The main customer record processing loop must continuously evaluate the end-of-file indicator before each iteration. Once the indicator is set to YES, the loop must terminate and no further customer records will be read or displayed.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The processing loop must exit immediately and no further customer records will be read or processed

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been attempted on the Customer File
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation completes and the file status is evaluated — where a status of successful indicates a record was read, a status of end-of-file indicates no more records exist, and any other status indicates an unexpected error condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the read was successful, the customer record is made available for display; if end-of-file is reached, the reading loop is flagged to stop; if an unexpected error occurred, error handling is triggered

rules.rule_name: Display Error Message on Unexpected Customer Record Read Failure
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error is encountered while reading a customer record (i.e., the file status is neither successful nor end-of-file), a descriptive error message must be immediately displayed to notify that the Customer File read has failed.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been attempted on the Customer File and the file status is neither a successful read nor an end-of-file condition

acceptance_criteria.Then: The error message 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE' is displayed

rules.rule_name: Capture and Display Customer File Status Details on Read Error
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected read error occurs on the Customer File, the file status details must be captured and displayed in a formatted manner to support error diagnosis. The display format differs based on whether the status is non-numeric or begins with '9' (system error) versus a standard numeric status code.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted file status is displayed with the label 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the four-character formatted status value, providing full visibility of the error condition

rules.rule_name: Trigger Abnormal Program Termination on Customer File Read Error

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unexpected error has occurred while reading the Customer File and both the error message and file status details have been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The abnormal termination sequence is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'ABENDING PROGRAM' is displayed and the program is immediately terminated abnormally, halting all further customer record processing

rules.rule_name: Determine File Status Code Format Type
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the file status error details, the system must determine whether the captured file status code is a standard numeric status or a special/non-numeric status, as each type requires a different formatting approach for accurate error reporting.

acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the file status code prior to displaying error details
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file status code is non-numeric OR the first character of the status code is '9' (indicating a special/vendor-specific status), the system must route to non-numeric status formatting; otherwise, if the status code is fully numeric and does not begin with '9', the system must route to standard numeric status formatting

rules.rule_name: Format and Display Special or Non-Numeric File Status Details
rules.rule_description: When the file status code is identified as non-numeric or special (first character is '9'), the status must be formatted using a binary conversion technique to accurately represent the extended status information before displaying it.

acceptance_criteria.When: The system formats the error status for display

rules.rule_name: Format and Display Standard Numeric File Status Details
rules.rule_description: When the file status code is a standard numeric value (not special or non-numeric), it must be formatted into a four-character display field and shown with a standard label so the error status is clearly communicated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format and Display Numeric File Status Details

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file status code has been determined to be fully numeric and does not begin with '9'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system formats the error status for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) initialize the four-character display status field to '0000', (2) overlay the last two characters of that display field with the two-character numeric status code, and (3) display the message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the fully formatted four-character status field

rules.rule_name: Announce and Execute Program Termination After Customer File Open Failure
rules.rule_description: After all error details have been reported for a Customer File open failure, the system must announce that it is terminating and then invoke an abnormal termination to stop all further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Program Termination Notice: 'ABENDING PROGRAM'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer File open error message and status details have been fully displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds to terminate due to the unrecoverable Customer File open failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'ABENDING PROGRAM' to announce the termination, and then invoke the abnormal termination routine (CEE3ABD) with termination code 999 to immediately stop all program execution

acceptance_criteria.When: The file status code is either non-numeric OR the first character of the file status code begins with '9' (indicating a system-level error)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The status is classified as a system-level or non-numeric error and must be formatted using the extended error status format; otherwise it is treated as a standard numeric file status code

rules.rule_name: Format System-Level Extended Error Status for Display
rules.rule_description: When a file status code is non-numeric or begins with '9', the two parts of the status code (primary status character and secondary binary status value) are combined into an extended display format to capture the full system-level error detail.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format as System-Level Extended Error Status Combine Status Code Parts into Display Format

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file status code has been identified as non-numeric or as a system-level error code beginning with '9'
acceptance_criteria.When: The extended error status is being formatted for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first character of the file status code (IO-STAT1) is placed into the first position of the display field; the second part of the file status code (IO-STAT2) is converted to its binary numeric equivalent and stored as the extended error number; both parts are combined into a single four-character display field (IO-STATUS-04) representing the full system-level error status

rules.rule_name: Format Standard Numeric File Status for Display
rules.rule_description: When the file status code is a standard numeric value (not system-level), it is formatted into a four-character display field by placing the two-digit status code into the last two positions of the display field, with the first two positions set to zeros.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format as Standard Numeric File Status Place Status Code into Display Format

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file status code has been identified as a standard numeric status code (not non-numeric and not beginning with '9')
acceptance_criteria.When: The standard numeric file status is being formatted for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The display field (IO-STATUS-04) is initialized to '0000'; the two-digit numeric file status code (IO-STATUS) is placed into the third and fourth character positions of the display field, resulting in a four-character representation such as '0010' for end-of-file or '0012' for an error condition

rules.rule_name: Display System-Level Extended File Status Information
rules.rule_description: After formatting a system-level or non-numeric file status code into the extended display format, the complete formatted status information is displayed to support error diagnosis, prefixed with the label 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN'.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Formatted File Status Information FILE STATUS IS: NNNN followed by Status Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file status code has been identified as system-level or non-numeric and has been formatted into the extended four-character display field (IO-STATUS-04)
acceptance_criteria.When: The formatted system-level error status is ready for output
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the four-character extended status code (IO-STATUS-04) is displayed, providing the full system-level error detail for diagnosis

rules.rule_name: Display Standard Numeric File Status Information
rules.rule_description: After formatting a standard numeric file status code into the four-character display format, the complete formatted status information is displayed to support error diagnosis, prefixed with the label 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN'.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Formatted File Status Information FILE STATUS IS: NNNN followed by Status Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file status code has been identified as a standard numeric status code and has been formatted into the four-character display field (IO-STATUS-04) with leading zeros
acceptance_criteria.When: The formatted standard numeric status is ready for output
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the four-character formatted status code (IO-STATUS-04) is displayed, providing the standard file status detail for diagnosis

rules.rule_name: Customer File Close Failure Notification
rules.rule_description: When the customer file cannot be closed successfully after processing, an error message must be immediately displayed to notify that the customer file close operation has failed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Error Message: 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer file close operation has been attempted and the file status indicates an unsuccessful close (file status is not '00')
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects that the customer file did not close successfully
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the error message 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE' to the output to notify of the failure

rules.rule_name: Capture File Status for Close Error Reporting
rules.rule_description: When a customer file close error occurs, the file status code at the time of failure must be captured and retained so it can be included in the error report for diagnostic purposes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture File Status Code for Reporting

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer file close operation has failed and an error message has been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to report the details of the file close failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must capture and store the current customer file status code into the I/O status field so it is available for formatted error reporting

rules.rule_name: Determine File Status Code Format for Error Reporting
rules.rule_description: When reporting a customer file close error, the system must determine whether the captured file status code is a standard numeric status or a special non-numeric status, as each type requires a different formatting approach before display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is File Status Code Numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer file close error has occurred and the file status code has been captured
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the file status code to determine its type
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file status code is non-numeric OR the first character of the status code is '9' (indicating a special/extended status), the system must treat it as a special status code and apply special formatting; otherwise, if the file status code is fully numeric and does not begin with '9', the system must treat it as a standard numeric status code and apply standard formatting

rules.rule_name: Format Standard Numeric File Status for Display
rules.rule_description: When the file status code from a customer file close error is a standard numeric code (fully numeric and not beginning with '9'), it must be formatted into a four-character display field for clear error reporting.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format and Display Numeric File Status Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer file close error has occurred, the file status code has been captured, and the status code is determined to be fully numeric and does not begin with '9'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system formats the standard numeric file status code for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must initialize the four-character display status field to '0000', then place the two-character numeric file status code into the last two positions (positions 3 and 4) of the display field, resulting in a formatted four-character status value ready for output

rules.rule_name: Format Special Non-Numeric File Status for Display
rules.rule_description: When the file status code from a customer file close error is non-numeric or begins with '9' (indicating a special or extended error condition), it must be specially formatted by separating its two components into a four-character display field for accurate error reporting.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format and Display Non-Numeric File Status Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer file close error has occurred, the file status code has been captured, and the status code is either non-numeric or its first character is '9'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system formats the special file status code for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must place the first character of the file status code into the first position of the four-character display field, then convert the second character of the file status code into its binary numeric equivalent and store that value into the remaining portion of the display field, resulting in a formatted four-character status value that represents both components of the special status code

rules.rule_name: Display Formatted File Status Details
rules.rule_description: After the file status code has been formatted (either as a standard numeric or special non-numeric status), the formatted status details must be displayed to the output as part of the customer file close error report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Formatted File Status Details to Output

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer file close error has occurred and the file status code has been formatted into the four-character display field using either the standard or special formatting method
acceptance_criteria.When: The system outputs the file status details
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the four-character formatted file status value to the output, providing the complete status detail for the close error

rules.rule_name: Announce Program Abnormal Termination
rules.rule_description: Before the program is forcibly terminated due to a customer file close failure, a final notification message must be displayed to clearly indicate that the program is about to terminate abnormally.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display 'ABENDING PROGRAM' Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer file close error has been reported with the error message and formatted file status details already displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is about to initiate abnormal program termination
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'ABENDING PROGRAM' to the output as the final notification before termination is triggered

rules.rule_name: Abnormal Program Termination on Customer File Close Failure
rules.rule_description: When the customer file cannot be closed successfully and all error details have been reported, the program must be forcibly and abnormally terminated to prevent any further processing in an inconsistent state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Terminate Program Abnormally

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer file close operation has failed, the error message 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE' has been displayed, the formatted file status details have been displayed, and the 'ABENDING PROGRAM' message has been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the abnormal termination sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must invoke the abnormal termination routine with an abend code of 999 to immediately and forcibly stop all program execution, ensuring no further customer data processing occurs

rules.rule_name: Identify System-Level or Non-Numeric File Status Error
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the file status code represents a system-level or non-standard error condition, which requires special formatting, as opposed to a standard numeric status code that can be displayed directly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is File Status Code Non-Numeric OR System-Level Error Code Starting with 9?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A file operation has resulted in an error and the file status code is available for diagnosis
acceptance_criteria.When: The file status code is either non-numeric (cannot be interpreted as a number) OR the first character of the file status code is '9' (indicating a system-level error)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error is classified as a system-level or non-numeric error and must be formatted and displayed using the system-level error display path; otherwise it is treated as a standard numeric status code

rules.rule_name: Extract and Format System-Level File Status Details
rules.rule_description: When a system-level or non-numeric file error is detected, the status code is decomposed into its two parts: the first character is extracted directly, and the second part is converted into a numeric value to capture the system-specific error detail. Both parts are then combined into a formatted display area for output.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract First Character of Status Code / Convert Second Part of Status Code to Numeric Value for System Error Detail / Format Combined Status as System-Level Error Display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file status code has been identified as non-numeric or as a system-level error code beginning with '9'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system-level error formatting process is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first character of the file status code is extracted and placed into the first position of the formatted status display area; the second character/part of the status code is converted to its numeric binary equivalent and stored as the system error detail; both components are combined into a single formatted status display field (IO-STATUS-04) ready for output

rules.rule_name: Display System-Level File Status Information
rules.rule_description: After formatting the system-level file status details, the combined status information is displayed to support error diagnosis, clearly labelled to indicate it is a file status message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display System-Level File Status Information

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system-level file status details have been extracted and formatted into the display area (IO-STATUS-04)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system-level display step is reached
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the formatted system-level status code (IO-STATUS-04) is displayed to the output, providing full error detail for diagnosis

rules.rule_name: Initialize and Format Standard Numeric File Status for Display
rules.rule_description: When the file status code is a standard numeric value (not system-level and not non-numeric), the display area is first cleared to zeros and then the two-character numeric status code is placed into the last two positions of the four-character display field, ensuring consistent formatting for output.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Initialize Status Display Area to Zeros / Place Standard Numeric Status Code into Display Format

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file status code has been identified as a standard numeric status code (not non-numeric and not starting with '9')
acceptance_criteria.When: The standard numeric status formatting process is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The four-character status display area (IO-STATUS-04) is initialized to '0000'; the two-character numeric file status code (IO-STATUS) is then placed into positions 3 and 4 of the display area, resulting in a zero-padded four-character formatted status code ready for display

rules.rule_name: Display Standard Numeric File Status Information
rules.rule_description: After formatting the standard numeric file status code, the formatted status information is displayed to support error diagnosis, using the same label format as the system-level display for consistency.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Standard File Status Information

acceptance_criteria.Given: The standard numeric file status code has been formatted into the display area (IO-STATUS-04) with zero-padding
acceptance_criteria.When: The standard display step is reached
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the formatted standard numeric status code (IO-STATUS-04) is displayed to the output, providing the status detail for error diagnosis
