rules.rule_name: Display End of Program Execution Message
rules.rule_description: Upon successful completion of all customer record processing and file closure, the program must display a message confirming the end of its execution before returning control.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display End of Execution Message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBCUS01C'

acceptance_criteria.Given: All customer records have been successfully read and displayed, and the Customer File has been successfully closed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program has completed all its processing steps with no errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBCUS01C' to confirm successful completion of the program

rules.rule_name: Return Control to Calling Environment
rules.rule_description: After displaying the end-of-execution message, the program must formally return control back to the calling environment, signalling that all processing is complete and the program has ended normally.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return Control to Calling Environment

acceptance_criteria.Given: The end-of-execution message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBCUS01C' has been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program has finished all processing and is ready to exit
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is returned to the calling environment, marking the normal and complete end of the program

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File Display Program CBCUS01C is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBCUS01C' is displayed to the output before any file operations or customer record processing takes place

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Execution Start Announcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program announces the beginning of its execution by displaying a start message before any customer data processing begins.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has displayed its start message and is ready to begin customer record processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE) for sequential input reading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer File is opened in INPUT mode to allow sequential reading of all customer records, and the file open status is evaluated to determine if the operation was successful

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Open for Sequential Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Customer File (CUSTFILE) must be opened for sequential input reading as the first file operation before any customer records can be accessed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE) for input reading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open operation completes and the file status is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status indicates success (status code '00'), the application result is set to zero (AOK) and the program proceeds to the sequential record processing loop; otherwise, the application result is set to 12 (error) and the file open error reporting process is triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Open Success Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to open the Customer File, the program validates whether the file was opened successfully before proceeding to read customer records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program attempted to open the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE) and the file open operation did not return a successful status
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open failure is detected (application result is not AOK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE' is displayed, the file status is captured and displayed in a formatted status message prefixed with 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN', and the program is terminated abnormally by calling the system abend routine CEE3ABD with abend code 999

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Open Error Reporting and Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Customer File cannot be opened successfully, the program reports the error with the file status details and terminates abnormally, preventing any customer record processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File has been successfully opened for sequential reading and the End-of-File indicator is set to 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The sequential processing loop is active
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program continuously reads and processes customer records one at a time, repeating the read-and-display cycle until the End-of-File indicator is set to 'Y', at which point the loop terminates and the program proceeds to close the Customer File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Customer Record Processing Loop
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program processes all customer records sequentially in a continuous loop, reading and displaying each record until the end of the Customer File is reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The sequential customer record processing loop is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Each iteration of the loop begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the End-of-File indicator is 'N' (end of file not yet reached), the program proceeds to read the next customer record; if the End-of-File indicator is 'Y' (end of file reached), the loop exits and the program proceeds to close the Customer File

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Condition Check Before Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: At each iteration of the processing loop, the program checks whether the end of the Customer File has been reached before attempting to read the next record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The End-of-File indicator is 'N' and the program is within the sequential processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program executes a sequential read operation on the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next customer record is read from the Customer File into the CUSTOMER-RECORD data area, and the resulting file status is evaluated to determine whether the read was successful, end-of-file was reached, or an unexpected error occurred

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Sequential Customer Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program reads the next sequential customer record from the Customer File into the Customer Record data area for processing and display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file status returned from the read operation is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status is '00' (successful read), the application result is set to zero (AOK) and the customer record is displayed; if the file status is '10' (end of file), the application result is set to 16 (EOF) and the End-of-File indicator is set to 'Y' to stop the loop; if the file status is any other value (unexpected error), the application result is set to 12 (error) and the read error reporting process is triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Record Read Status Evaluation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each read operation, the program evaluates the file status to determine whether a customer record was successfully retrieved, the end of file was reached, or an unexpected error occurred.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation on the Customer File has returned a successful status (file status '00') and the CUSTOMER-RECORD data area has been populated with the retrieved record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The successful read is confirmed (application result is AOK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete contents of the CUSTOMER-RECORD are displayed to the output, and the processing loop continues to check for the next record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Successfully Retrieved Customer Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer record is successfully read from the Customer File, the complete customer record details are displayed to the output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation on the Customer File has returned an end-of-file status (file status '10'), setting the application result to 16 (EOF)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The application result is evaluated and identified as EOF (application result equals 16)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End-of-File indicator (END-OF-FILE) is set to 'Y', which causes the sequential processing loop to exit on its next iteration check, and the program proceeds to close the Customer File — no error is raised as end-of-file is the expected normal conclusion of processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Indicator Setting to Stop Processing Loop
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the read operation detects that there are no more customer records in the file, the End-of-File indicator is set to stop the processing loop gracefully.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation on the Customer File has returned a file status that is neither '00' (success) nor '10' (end of file), resulting in an application result of 12 (error)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The application result is evaluated and identified as neither AOK nor EOF
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The unexpected read error condition is confirmed and the read error reporting and program termination process is immediately triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unexpected Customer Record Read Error Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a read operation on the Customer File returns an unexpected error status (neither successful nor end-of-file), the error condition is detected and escalated for reporting and program termination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unexpected error has been detected during a sequential read operation on the Customer File (application result is 12, indicating neither a successful read nor end-of-file)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read error condition is confirmed and error reporting is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE' is displayed, the file status is captured and displayed in a formatted status message prefixed with 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN', and the program is terminated abnormally by calling the system abend routine CEE3ABD with abend code 999

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Read Error Reporting and Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading a customer record, the program reports the error with file status details and terminates abnormally to prevent processing of potentially corrupt or incomplete data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The sequential processing loop has exited because the End-of-File indicator was set to 'Y', indicating all customer records have been processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program executes the close operation on the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer File is closed and the resulting file status is evaluated to determine whether the close operation was successful or failed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Close After All Records Processed
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all customer records have been read and displayed (end of file reached), the Customer File must be properly closed to complete the processing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE) after all records have been processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file close operation completes and the file status is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status indicates success (status code '00'), the application result is set to zero (AOK) and the program proceeds to display the completion message and exit normally; otherwise, the application result is set to 12 (error) and the file close error reporting process is triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Close Success Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to close the Customer File, the program validates whether the file was closed successfully before announcing program completion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program attempted to close the Customer File (CUSTFILE-FILE) after completing all record processing and the file close operation did not return a successful status (application result is 12)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file close failure is detected (application result is not AOK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE' is displayed, the file status is captured and displayed in a formatted status message prefixed with 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN', and the program is terminated abnormally by calling the system abend routine CEE3ABD with abend code 999

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Close Error Reporting and Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Customer File cannot be closed successfully after all records have been processed, the program reports the error with file status details and terminates abnormally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All customer records have been read and displayed, and the Customer File has been successfully closed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches its normal completion point
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBCUS01C' is displayed to the output, and control is returned to the calling environment via GOBACK, signaling successful completion of the customer file display process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Completion Announcement and Normal Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful completion of all customer record processing and successful closure of the Customer File, the program announces its completion and returns control to the calling environment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File Display Program CBCUS01C has been invoked and is beginning execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes and before any customer file operations are performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBCUS01C' to confirm that program execution has begun

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Program Start Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Customer File Display Program begins execution, it must announce its start by displaying an identifiable program start message before any customer file processing takes place.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File processing is about to begin and no customer records have yet been read
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the Customer File opening sequence to prepare for sequential record retrieval
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer File is opened in read-only sequential access mode, making all customer records available for processing from the first record to the last

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Sequential Access Initiation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any customer records can be retrieved and processed, the Customer File must be opened to enable sequential reading from the beginning of the file through to the last record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An attempt has been made to open the Customer File for sequential reading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The result of the file open operation is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Customer File opened successfully, it is marked as ready for sequential record processing; if the Customer File could not be opened for any reason, it is flagged as unavailable and error handling is triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Availability Verification
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to open the Customer File, the program must verify whether the file is available and accessible. A successful open confirms the file is ready; any other outcome indicates the file is unavailable for processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File open operation has been evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer File has been confirmed as successfully opened with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer File is marked as available and ready, and control is returned to the main process to begin sequential customer record retrieval

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Ready for Record Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Customer File has been confirmed as successfully opened, it is designated as ready, allowing the main processing loop to begin retrieving customer records sequentially.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File open operation has been evaluated and the file could not be opened successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open failure condition is confirmed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE' is displayed, followed by the detailed file status information formatted as a 4-character status code prefixed with 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN', so that the reason for the Customer File being unavailable is clearly communicated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Open Failure Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Customer File cannot be opened, a descriptive error message must be displayed along with the specific file status details to identify the nature of the failure, enabling diagnosis of why the customer data is inaccessible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File could not be opened and the file open error message with status details has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program determines it cannot continue without access to the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program is immediately terminated abnormally with abend code 999, halting all further customer record processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Termination on Customer File Open Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Customer File cannot be opened, the program cannot proceed with any customer record processing. The program must be immediately and abnormally terminated to prevent any further processing without valid customer data access.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record processing loop is active and the system is about to begin or continue an iteration
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End-of-File Indicator is evaluated at the start of each loop iteration
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the End-of-File Indicator equals 'Y', the loop exits immediately and processing proceeds to close the Customer File; if the End-of-File Indicator does not equal 'Y', the loop continues to the next check

all_rules.Rule_Name: Loop Entry Control - Check If All Customer Records Have Been Processed
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before each iteration of the customer record processing loop, the system checks whether the end-of-file indicator has been set, to determine if all customer records have already been read and no further processing is needed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The End-of-File Indicator has been confirmed as not equal to 'Y' and the loop is continuing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the End-of-File Indicator is explicitly equal to 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the End-of-File Indicator equals 'N', the system proceeds to read the next customer record; if the End-of-File Indicator is not 'N', the system loops back to the primary end-of-file check without reading any record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Loop Safety Guard - Confirm File Still Has Unread Records Before Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: As a secondary safety check within the loop, the system confirms the End-of-File Indicator is explicitly set to 'N' before attempting to read the next customer record, preventing any unintended read attempts.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File is open, the End-of-File Indicator is 'N', and there are potentially more customer records to be read
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the next sequential record from the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer record details are loaded into the Customer Record area and the outcome of the read operation (success, end of file, or error) is captured for subsequent decision-making

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Customer Record Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system retrieves the next available customer record sequentially from the Customer File, loading the full customer record details into the active customer record area for processing and display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation completes successfully, confirming a valid customer record has been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The full Customer Record details are displayed immediately upon successful retrieval; additionally, since the End-of-File Indicator remains 'N' after a successful read, the Customer Record details are displayed a second time in the main processing loop, resulting in each customer record being displayed twice per successful read

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Customer Record Read - Display Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer record is successfully retrieved from the Customer File, the system displays the full customer record details. Due to the program structure, each successfully read customer record is displayed twice — once immediately upon successful retrieval and once again in the main processing loop after the read operation returns.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation returns an end-of-file condition, indicating no further customer records exist in the file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End-of-File Indicator is set to 'Y', which causes the processing loop to exit on its next iteration check, and no customer record is displayed for this condition

all_rules.Rule_Name: End of Customer File Detection - Stop Reading Loop
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system determines that there are no more customer records available in the Customer File, it marks the End-of-File Indicator to signal that all records have been processed and the reading loop should terminate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation returns any outcome other than success or end-of-file, indicating an unexpected failure condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE', displays the file status details, and terminates the program abnormally — no further customer records are read or displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unexpected Customer File Read Failure - Report Error and Terminate
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading a customer record — any condition other than a successful read or a normal end-of-file — the system reports the error and terminates the program abnormally to prevent processing of incomplete or corrupt customer data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record processing loop is evaluating the End-of-File Indicator
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End-of-File Indicator equals 'Y', confirming all customer records have been read
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The processing loop terminates and the system proceeds to close the Customer File, with no further customer records being read or displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Loop Exit and Transition to File Closure
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the End-of-File Indicator is confirmed as 'Y', the customer record processing loop exits and control is passed to the file closure process, ensuring the Customer File is properly closed after all records have been processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File has been successfully opened and is ready for sequential reading, and the end-of-file indicator is set to 'N' (more records may exist)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests the next sequential customer record from the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next customer record is read from the Customer File and its data is loaded into the customer record structure, making all customer fields available for processing and display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Customer Record Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system retrieves the next available customer record sequentially from the Customer File and loads it into the customer record structure for downstream processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed against the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer File returns a successful read result indicating the record was found and retrieved without any issues
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer record is confirmed as successfully retrieved into the customer record structure, the processing result is marked as successful (no error), and the full customer record details are displayed to the output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Customer Record Retrieved
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer record is successfully read from the Customer File, the record is confirmed as retrieved and its contents are immediately displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed against the Customer File and the read was not successful
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer File signals that the end of the file has been reached and there are no more customer records available to read
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The processing result is marked as end-of-file, and the end-of-file indicator is set to 'Y', signalling the processing loop to stop reading and proceed to file closure — no error is raised as this is the expected normal conclusion of processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Detection — No More Customer Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Customer File signals that there are no more records to read, the system marks the end-of-file indicator to stop further reading and gracefully conclude the processing loop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed against the Customer File and the read was not successful
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer File returns an unexpected error result that is neither a successful record retrieval nor a normal end-of-file condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The processing result is marked as an error, the message 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE' is displayed, the file status details are displayed for diagnostic purposes, and the program is terminated abnormally — no further customer records are processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unexpected Customer Record Read Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading a customer record — one that is neither a successful read nor a normal end-of-file — the system treats it as a critical failure, displays a diagnostic error message, and terminates the program abnormally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been attempted on the Customer File to retrieve the next customer record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation completes and the file status is evaluated — status '00' indicates a successful record retrieval, status '10' indicates end of file has been reached, and any other status indicates a read failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Only if the read status is '00' (successful record retrieved) is the record considered valid and eligible for display; if the status is '10' (end of file) or any other value (read failure), the record is not eligible for display and processing continues to the next step without displaying any record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Successful Customer Record Read Before Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to read a customer record, the system must verify that the read operation completed successfully before proceeding to display the record. Only a fully successful retrieval qualifies the record for output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record read attempt has been performed and the read paragraph has completed execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The main processing loop evaluates the End-of-File indicator after returning from the read operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the End-of-File indicator is 'N' (more records are available and the last read was successful), the customer record is eligible for display; if the End-of-File indicator is 'Y' (end of file has been reached during the read), the customer record is not displayed and the loop proceeds toward termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Verify End-of-File Indicator Before Displaying Customer Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying a customer record in the main processing loop, the system must confirm that the end-of-file condition has not been reached. This prevents displaying stale or invalid data after the last record has been processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully read from the Customer File (read status is '00') and the End-of-File indicator remains 'N' after the read operation completes
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Both the successful read condition and the active (non-end-of-file) processing condition are confirmed true in the main processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete customer record details are displayed to the output in full; after display, processing continues to attempt reading the next customer record in the sequence

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Full Customer Record Details After Successful Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer File and the end-of-file condition has not been triggered, the complete customer record details must be printed to the output. This is the core output action of the customer file display process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been attempted on the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer File signals that there are no more records available to read (end-of-file status is returned)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must recognise and record an end-of-file condition internally, distinguishing it from a successful record retrieval and from any unexpected read error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect End-of-File Condition After Read Attempt
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a read attempt is made on the Customer File and no more records exist, the system must recognise the end-of-file condition and flag it internally so that downstream logic can stop the processing loop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The end-of-file condition has been detected after a read attempt on the Customer File (no more customer records exist)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the end-of-file condition is active (internal result code equals end-of-file value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end-of-file indicator must be set to YES, signalling that no further customer records should be requested

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set End-of-File Indicator to Stop Processing Loop
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the end-of-file condition has been detected on the Customer File, the end-of-file indicator must be explicitly set to YES so that the main processing loop knows to stop requesting further customer records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record processing loop is active and has been reading customer records sequentially
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file indicator is evaluated and found to be YES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The processing loop must exit immediately and no further customer records will be read or processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Exit Customer Record Processing Loop When End-of-File Indicator Is Set
all_rules.Rule_Description: The main customer record processing loop must continuously evaluate the end-of-file indicator before each iteration. Once the indicator is set to YES, the loop must terminate and no further customer records will be read or displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been attempted on the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record is successfully retrieved (end-of-file indicator remains NO after the read)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The retrieved customer record must be displayed and the processing loop must continue to attempt reading the next customer record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Customer Record Processing When Record Successfully Retrieved
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer record is successfully read from the Customer File and the end-of-file indicator remains NO, the system must continue processing by displaying the retrieved customer record and then looping back to read the next record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been attempted on the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation completes and the file status is evaluated — where a status of successful indicates a record was read, a status of end-of-file indicates no more records exist, and any other status indicates an unexpected error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the read was successful, the customer record is made available for display; if end-of-file is reached, the reading loop is flagged to stop; if an unexpected error occurred, error handling is triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Customer Record Read Outcome
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer record read is attempted, the outcome must be classified as either a successful read, an end-of-file condition, or an unexpected error, so that the appropriate subsequent action is taken.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been attempted on the Customer File and the file status is neither a successful read nor an end-of-file condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The unexpected error condition is confirmed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error Message on Unexpected Customer Record Read Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error is encountered while reading a customer record (i.e., the file status is neither successful nor end-of-file), a descriptive error message must be immediately displayed to notify that the Customer File read has failed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unexpected error has occurred while reading the Customer File and the error message has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file status details are being captured for reporting — if the file status is non-numeric or the first character of the status is '9', the status is formatted as a system-level code combining the first status character and a binary representation of the second status character; otherwise, the last two characters of a four-character display field are populated with the numeric status value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted file status is displayed with the label 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the four-character formatted status value, providing full visibility of the error condition

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture and Display Customer File Status Details on Read Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected read error occurs on the Customer File, the file status details must be captured and displayed in a formatted manner to support error diagnosis. The display format differs based on whether the status is non-numeric or begins with '9' (system error) versus a standard numeric status code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unexpected error has occurred while reading the Customer File and both the error message and file status details have been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The abnormal termination sequence is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message 'ABENDING PROGRAM' is displayed and the program is immediately terminated abnormally, halting all further customer record processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Abnormal Program Termination on Customer File Read Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After an unexpected read error on the Customer File has been reported and file status details have been displayed, the program must be forcibly terminated abnormally to prevent further processing on a corrupted or inaccessible data source.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All customer records have been read and the end of the Customer File has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer File is closed and the program proceeds to the completion stage

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Customer File After All Records Are Processed
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all customer records have been read and processed, the Customer File must be formally closed to complete the processing cycle and release the file resource.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the Customer File after processing all customer records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file closure operation completes and the resulting file status is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status indicates success (file closed without errors), the program proceeds to normal program completion; otherwise, the program handles the closure failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Successful Closure of Customer File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to close the Customer File, the program must verify that the closure was completed successfully. A successful closure confirms the file was properly finalized and all data integrity is maintained.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the Customer File and the closure was not successful
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file status does not indicate a successful closure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the error message 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE' along with the detailed file status information, and then terminates the program abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Customer File Close Failure and Terminate Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Customer File cannot be closed successfully, the program must notify the user with an error message including the file status details, and then terminate the program abnormally to prevent data integrity issues.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File open operation has been attempted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer File does not open successfully (file status is not '00')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the error message 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE' to signal that the Customer File could not be opened

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer File Open Failure Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Customer File cannot be opened successfully, an error message must be immediately displayed to notify that the Customer File open operation has failed before any further error details are reported.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File has failed to open and an error message has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to report the detailed error status
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current Customer File status code must be captured into the error reporting status field (IO-STATUS) so it is available for formatted display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Customer File Status for Error Reporting
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Customer File open failure is detected, the current file status code must be captured and retained so it can be used for detailed error reporting to support diagnosis of the failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File status code has been captured into the error reporting status field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the file status code prior to displaying error details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status code is non-numeric OR the first character of the status code is '9' (indicating a special/vendor-specific status), the system must route to non-numeric status formatting; otherwise, if the status code is fully numeric and does not begin with '9', the system must route to standard numeric status formatting

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine File Status Code Format Type
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the file status error details, the system must determine whether the captured file status code is a standard numeric status or a special/non-numeric status, as each type requires a different formatting approach for accurate error reporting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file status code has been determined to be non-numeric OR its first character is '9'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the error status for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) place the first character of the status code into the first position of the display status field, (2) convert the second character of the status code through a binary intermediate field to derive a numeric representation, (3) place that numeric value into the display status field, and (4) display the message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the fully formatted four-character status field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Special or Non-Numeric File Status Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file status code is identified as non-numeric or special (first character is '9'), the status must be formatted using a binary conversion technique to accurately represent the extended status information before displaying it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file status code has been determined to be fully numeric and does not begin with '9'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the error status for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) initialize the four-character display status field to '0000', (2) overlay the last two characters of that display field with the two-character numeric status code, and (3) display the message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the fully formatted four-character status field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Standard Numeric File Status Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file status code is a standard numeric value (not special or non-numeric), it must be formatted into a four-character display field and shown with a standard label so the error status is clearly communicated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File open error message and status details have been fully displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to terminate due to the unrecoverable Customer File open failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'ABENDING PROGRAM' to announce the termination, and then invoke the abnormal termination routine (CEE3ABD) with termination code 999 to immediately stop all program execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Announce and Execute Program Termination After Customer File Open Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all error details have been reported for a Customer File open failure, the system must announce that it is terminating and then invoke an abnormal termination to stop all further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File is open and being read sequentially, and a read operation has been attempted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file read operation returns a status that is neither successful (status '00') nor end-of-file (status '10')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the error message 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE' to the output to notify the operator that an unexpected error has occurred during customer record retrieval

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Unexpected Customer File Read Error and Notify
all_rules.Rule_Description: When reading the Customer File results in an outcome that is neither a successful read nor an end-of-file condition, the program must immediately identify this as an unexpected error and display a descriptive error message to alert the operator.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unexpected error has occurred while reading the Customer File and the error message 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE' has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program proceeds to report the error details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current Customer File status code must be captured into the I/O status reporting field so that it is available for formatting and display to the operator

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Customer File Status Code for Error Reporting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon detecting an unexpected read error on the Customer File, the current file status code must be captured and preserved so it can be formatted and displayed as part of the error reporting process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File status code has been captured for error reporting
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the captured file status code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status code is non-numeric OR the first character of the file status is '9' (indicating a system-level error), the program must route to system-level status formatting; otherwise, if the file status is a standard numeric value, the program must route to standard status formatting

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine File Status Type for Error Formatting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before formatting the file status details for display, the program must evaluate whether the captured file status represents a system-level or non-numeric error versus a standard numeric file status, as each type requires a different formatting approach.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File status code has been determined to be either non-numeric or a system-level error (first character is '9')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program formats the file status details for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first character of the file status must be placed in the first position of the display status field; the second status character must be converted to its binary numeric equivalent and placed in the remaining positions of the display status field, producing a four-character formatted status code for output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format System-Level File Status Details for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file status indicates a system-level or non-numeric error, the status details must be formatted in a specific way that correctly represents the system error code by combining the first status character with a binary-converted representation of the second status character.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File status code has been determined to be a standard numeric value (not a system-level or non-numeric error)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program formats the file status details for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The four-character display status field must be initialized to '0000', and the two-character numeric file status code must be placed into the third and fourth positions of the display field, producing a four-character formatted status code for output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Standard Numeric File Status Details for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file status is a standard numeric value, the status details must be formatted by placing the two-character numeric status code into the last two positions of a four-character display field, with the first two positions set to zeros.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File error status code has been formatted into a four-character display field (either via system-level or standard numeric formatting)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program outputs the error status details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed immediately by the four-character formatted file status code, providing the operator with the precise file status information for diagnosis

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Formatted File Status Code to Output
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the file status details have been formatted (either as system-level or standard numeric), the formatted four-character status code must be displayed to the output with a descriptive label so the operator can identify the exact nature of the file error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File read error message and formatted file status code have been displayed to the operator
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program proceeds to terminate due to the unrecoverable Customer File read error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'ABENDING PROGRAM' to notify the operator of the abnormal termination, and then invoke the system abnormal termination service (CEE3ABD) with abend code 999, causing the program to terminate abnormally and ensuring the failure is captured in the system job log

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Termination Notice and Abnormally Terminate Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the file status details have been displayed, the program must notify the operator that it is terminating abnormally and then invoke the system abnormal termination service to end the program with a specific abend code, ensuring the failure is recorded and visible in the job output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer file close operation has been attempted and the file status indicates an unsuccessful close (file status is not '00')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects that the customer file did not close successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the error message 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE' to the output to notify of the failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Close Failure Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the customer file cannot be closed successfully after processing, an error message must be immediately displayed to notify that the customer file close operation has failed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer file close operation has failed and an error message has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to report the details of the file close failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must capture and store the current customer file status code into the I/O status field so it is available for formatted error reporting

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture File Status for Close Error Reporting
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer file close error occurs, the file status code at the time of failure must be captured and retained so it can be included in the error report for diagnostic purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer file close error has occurred and the file status code has been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the file status code to determine its type
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status code is non-numeric OR the first character of the status code is '9' (indicating a special/extended status), the system must treat it as a special status code and apply special formatting; otherwise, if the file status code is fully numeric and does not begin with '9', the system must treat it as a standard numeric status code and apply standard formatting

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine File Status Code Format for Error Reporting
all_rules.Rule_Description: When reporting a customer file close error, the system must determine whether the captured file status code is a standard numeric status or a special non-numeric status, as each type requires a different formatting approach before display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer file close error has occurred, the file status code has been captured, and the status code is determined to be fully numeric and does not begin with '9'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the standard numeric file status code for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must initialize the four-character display status field to '0000', then place the two-character numeric file status code into the last two positions (positions 3 and 4) of the display field, resulting in a formatted four-character status value ready for output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Standard Numeric File Status for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file status code from a customer file close error is a standard numeric code (fully numeric and not beginning with '9'), it must be formatted into a four-character display field for clear error reporting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer file close error has occurred, the file status code has been captured, and the status code is either non-numeric or its first character is '9'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the special file status code for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must place the first character of the file status code into the first position of the four-character display field, then convert the second character of the file status code into its binary numeric equivalent and store that value into the remaining portion of the display field, resulting in a formatted four-character status value that represents both components of the special status code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Special Non-Numeric File Status for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file status code from a customer file close error is non-numeric or begins with '9' (indicating a special or extended error condition), it must be specially formatted by separating its two components into a four-character display field for accurate error reporting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer file close error has occurred and the file status code has been formatted into the four-character display field using either the standard or special formatting method
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system outputs the file status details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the four-character formatted file status value to the output, providing the complete status detail for the close error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Formatted File Status Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the file status code has been formatted (either as a standard numeric or special non-numeric status), the formatted status details must be displayed to the output as part of the customer file close error report.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer file close error has been reported with the error message and formatted file status details already displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is about to initiate abnormal program termination
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'ABENDING PROGRAM' to the output as the final notification before termination is triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Announce Program Abnormal Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before the program is forcibly terminated due to a customer file close failure, a final notification message must be displayed to clearly indicate that the program is about to terminate abnormally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer file close operation has failed, the error message 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE' has been displayed, the formatted file status details have been displayed, and the 'ABENDING PROGRAM' message has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the abnormal termination sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must invoke the abnormal termination routine with an abend code of 999 to immediately and forcibly stop all program execution, ensuring no further customer data processing occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Abnormal Program Termination on Customer File Close Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the customer file cannot be closed successfully and all error details have been reported, the program must be forcibly and abnormally terminated to prevent any further processing in an inconsistent state.

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program has finished all processing and is ready to exit

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to Calling Environment

description:
CBCUS01C is a batch COBOL program within the CardDemo application that sequentially reads all records from an indexed customer data file (CUSTFILE) and displays each customer record to the system output. The program opens the customer file, iterates through every record until end-of-file is reached, prints each customer record, and then closes the file upon completion. This is a Main/Driver program with no external program calls other than an abend utility, and it operates independently without any CICS, DB2, IMS, or MQ interactions.
- **Execution Environment**: Batch - **Database Access**: VSAM (Indexed) - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Display a message indicating the start of program execution for CBCUS01C 2: Open Customer File - Open the indexed customer data file in sequential access mode to prepare for reading all customer records 3: Sequential Customer Record Processing Loop - Continuously read and process customer records one by one until all records in the file have been read (end of file reached) 4: Read Next Customer Record - Read the next sequential customer record from the indexed customer file into the customer record structure 5: Display Customer Record - Print/display the customer record details to the output after each successful read 6: End of File Detection - Detect when there are no more customer records to read and set the end-of-file indicator to stop the processing loop 7: Read Error Detection - Identify and handle unexpected errors encountered while reading customer records, triggering error reporting and program termination 8: Close Customer File - Close the customer data file after all records have been read and processed 9: File Open Error Reporting - Display an error message with file status details when the customer file cannot be opened successfully, then terminate the program 10: File Read Error Reporting - Display an error message with file status details when an unexpected error occurs reading the customer file, then terminate the program 11: File Close Error Reporting - Display an error message with file status details when the customer file cannot be closed successfully, then terminate the program 12: Program Completion - Display a message indicating the end of program execution and return control to the calling environment
